why:
LANDED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 R8): renamed to `GoalUuid`, rclrs's name, with this name kept one release as a `#[deprecated]` type alias (re-exported from `nros_core`, `nros_node`, `nros` and its prelude); every in-tree caller moved. PRIOR ROW: the 16-byte goal id, with `zero` / `is_zero` / `from_counter` and the two framing constants (`UUID_LEN`, `SEQ_PREFIX_LEN = 0`) that RFC-0069 pinned when the extra CDR header came out. `from_counter` is the RTOS half: a board with no entropy source still needs distinct goal ids. rclrs 0.5.1 ships NO action API at all -- the recorded surface has zero action, goal or feedback items -- so every action item in our Rust API is ours-only by construction rather than by an RTOS need. Ours mirror rclcpp_action's and `action_msgs`' concepts, and they are shared with our C and C++ surfaces (`rclc_goal_status_t`, `nros::GoalStatus`). The convergence point is whenever rclrs grows actions; until then there is nothing to be a divergence FROM.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. W4 F14, and this row's central factual claim is now FALSE — RE-VERDICTED extension -> rename.

The sentence above says "rclrs 0.5.1 ships NO action API at all — the recorded surface has zero action, goal or feedback items". The recorded surface is rclrs **0.7.0** (`docs/reference/api-surface/rclrs.json`, ref `0c62d76`) and it carries 26 action/goal records, `rclrs::GoalUuid` among them. The claim was true of the pin it was written against and was never re-read when the pin moved — the drift class issue 1042 is about, inside the ledger.

So there IS a counterpart: ours is `GoalId { pub uuid: [u8; 16] }` (`packages/core/nros-core/src/action.rs`), upstream's is `rclrs::GoalUuid`. Both are a 16-byte newtype; the name differs for no platform reason. `extension` asserts "ROS 2 has none", which is not true, and the honest verdict is `rename` — the same correction `rust:nros_fatal` took when rclrs's log macros were found.

The RTOS content of the row stands and is not deleted: `from_counter` exists because a board with no entropy source still needs distinct goal ids, and `UUID_LEN` / `SEQ_PREFIX_LEN` are RFC-0069's framing constants. HOW A USER FINDS OUT: COMPILE ERROR — a ported rclrs file names upstream's identifier and it does not resolve. That is the good failure mode, which is why this is a finding about the RECORD rather than about the user's experience: the row must not claim a constraint it does not have. No disposition is written; which spelling survives is the phase-417 stage-6 rename decision, and a disposition entered here would pre-empt it. RFC-0036 forbids recording a PREFERENCE as a divergence, so this row says which it is rather than leaving the reader to infer it.
